title: The Cell Membrane
subtitle: A selective electrical boundary
learningObjectives: Describe the phospholipid membrane as a selectively permeable electrical boundary.
Explain how pumps, channels and receptors maintain excitability.
Relate membrane targets to medication, electrolyte and channelopathy effects.

sections.explainSimply: The membrane is the cell’s flexible skin. It decides what can pass and helps keep the inside electrically different from the outside.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Ion gradients across the membrane make neural signalling possible. Channels, pumps and receptors translate chemical and electrical events into cellular responses.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: The phospholipid bilayer is selectively permeable. Na+/K+-ATPase maintains sodium and potassium gradients, while ligand-gated and voltage-gated channels alter membrane conductance and excitability.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A secure border with gates, scanners and staff who use energy to keep traffic moving in the correct direction.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Many psychoactive medications act at membrane receptors, transporters or ion channels rather than changing brain structure directly.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Channelopathies, toxins and electrolyte disturbance can produce seizures, confusion, weakness or altered arousal.
sections.clinicalPearl: A neuron’s “decision” to fire emerges from thousands of membrane events summing over time and space.
sections.practicalExample: A change in extracellular potassium alters the electrochemical gradient across neuronal membranes. The resulting shift in excitability can affect consciousness, muscle function and seizure risk.
sections.limitationsCautions: Membrane mechanisms are necessary but not sufficient explanations for complex symptoms. The same channel or receptor can have different effects across cell types and circuits.

quizBank.question: What maintains the major sodium and potassium gradients?
quizBank.explanation: The sodium-potassium pump uses ATP to preserve the gradients that support resting potential and action potentials.
